unit: WF4 Integrity Guard BLANK_ACTION_ID synthetic-key distinct count
description: Two separate Action rows with a blank action_id (whitespace-only, so they survive the Load Actions truthy filter) must each contribute their OWN synthetic ambiguous-id key '#blank@<snapshot_index>', so integrity_conflict_count is 2 — not 1 (a constant '#blank@' key would collapse both blanks onto one ambiguous id) and not 3, the raw conflict-record count (the second blank row is also missing its idempotency_key, so one extra BLANK_IDEMPOTENCY_KEY record rides along). The APPROVAL route keeps the per-action_id duplicate block OFF the blank id, leaving exactly the two BLANK_ACTION_ID records and the one BLANK_IDEMPOTENCY_KEY record.
why_it_exists: harness/FINDINGS.md section 1, closed 2026-08-28 (the syntactic count half; notice half is D-COUNT-01). The fix counts DISTINCT in-scope action_ids: `const id = S(c.action_id); if (id) ambiguousIds[id] = true; ... if (c.code === 'BLANK_ACTION_ID') ambiguousIds['#blank@' + c.snapshot_index] = true;`. A row with no id cannot be counted by id by definition, so it is counted by a synthetic key that must be unique PER ROW. If that key dropped the snapshot_index, two blank rows would collapse to one ambiguous id (count 1); if the counter reverted to conflicts.length, the extra BLANK_IDEMPOTENCY_KEY record would inflate the answer to the raw record count (3). This scenario is the only one in the suite that has blank action ids at all: every existing WF4 integrity scenario uses non-blank ids, so the synthetic-key branch is otherwise never reached.
assertions: two blank action_id rows (whitespace-only, so they survive the Load Actions truthy filter) each get their own synthetic key '#blank@<snapshot_index>' — '#blank@1' and '#blank@2' — so integrity_conflict_count is 2
the count is NOT 1: a constant '#blank@' key without the snapshot_index would collapse both blanks onto one ambiguous id
the count is NOT the raw record count (3): the second blank row is also missing its idempotency_key, so a BLANK_IDEMPOTENCY_KEY conflict record is reported alongside the two BLANK_ACTION_ID records
the reason string reads '2 ambiguous action(s) found, reported as 3 conflict record(s).'
integrity_code is BLANK_ACTION_ID: the two equal-severity blanks tie and the strictly-less-than scan keeps the earlier push as the headline
the APPROVAL route scopes the per-action_id duplicate block to the approval's single action id, so the blank id never also fires DUPLICATE_ACTION_ID
the Build Draft Context branch is never reached
the passthrough fields (route, chat_id, dry_run, passthrough_marker) survive onto the halt item
